definition: In a multi-hit combo, the anticipation-action-follow-through cycle is not repeated in full for every individual hit - intermediate hits chain anticipation directly into action and then straight into the NEXT hit's anticipation, with a full follow-through beat reserved for only the LAST hit in the chain, where its 'what happened after' role (staggering, flying back, a finishing move) actually has room to play out uninterrupted.
purpose: Keep a combo's pacing fast and continuous while still giving the sequence exactly one point (its end) where the audience gets a beat to register the outcome, rather than either omitting follow-through everywhere or awkwardly pausing after every single hit to give each one its own.
visible_effect: A rapid anticipation-action, anticipation-action... cadence through the body of the combo with no dedicated recovery pose between hits, followed by one clearly held follow-through pose (or an escalated finishing beat, e.g. a suplex) only after the final hit lands.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Keeps a combo reading as one continuous, escalating exchange rather than a series of separate, individually-punctuated attacks - the payoff and reaction are concentrated where they matter most (the combo's outcome) instead of being diluted across every hit.
physical_interpretation: A pacing convention rather than a physical claim - real consecutive strikes do have some recovery between them, but this technique compresses or omits drawing it explicitly for every intermediate hit in favour of pacing.
use_cases: any planned multi-hit attack sequence (a combo, a flurry) where continuous pacing across the whole sequence matters more than punctuating every individual hit
a finishing move or escalated final beat (the source's own example: ending a punch combo with a suplex) that specifically needs the follow-through's held reaction time to land
non_use_cases: a combo where each individual hit's outcome needs to be independently readable (a fighting game where each hit can be independently blocked, countered, or reacted to by the player) - there, at least a minimal follow-through/recovery cue per hit may be needed for fairness or readability, not only at the end
a single, non-chained attack, where the full three-part cycle applies normally with no deferral
interactions: layered_anticipation / startup_frame_budget / recovery_weight_substitution / implied_zero_frame_anticipation / follow_through_backfill_hold (W01's own anticipation ladder) - that chain already runs from 'spend frames before the action' to 'spend them after it instead' for a SINGLE action under a tight budget; this entry is the analogous compression applied across a whole MULTI-HIT SEQUENCE rather than within one action

overshoot_recoil_settle_pose_sequence (this batch, video 31) - the deferred final follow-through this entry describes is exactly where that card's overshoot/recoil/settle triad would play out in full, since it is the one beat in the combo actually given room for it

style_variations.game_combat: a player-facing combo system may need to relax this compression per hit specifically so each hit stays independently reactable - noted directly under non_use_cases

cadence_representation: Not represented as a named pattern: `ai/plan.js segmentPhases`/`TEMPLATES` name a single action's own phase order (anticipation, action, follow_through, recovery, settle) but has no concept of a MULTI-ACTION sequence where an intermediate action's own follow_through/recovery phases are omitted or compressed because another action immediately follows. Authoring a five-hit combo today would mean five separate `authorMotion` calls with no shared awareness that only the last one should get a full settle.
control_surface: None - each `authorMotion` call is independent; nothing currently coordinates phase omission across a sequence of calls.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Partially buildable: given a declared sequence of actions with markers, `ai/events.js` could in principle check whether intermediate actions' follow_through/recovery phases are indeed compressed relative to the final one's, but nothing currently reasons across multiple authored motions as one combo unit.
generation_or_modification_methods: None - no strategy authors a multi-hit sequence as a single unit with this deferral rule built in.
failure_modes: giving every intermediate hit in a combo its own full follow-through, breaking the sequence's continuous pacing and making it feel like separate attacks rather than one escalating exchange
deferring follow-through so completely that even the FINAL hit lacks one, leaving the whole combo's outcome unclear
roblox_considerations: None beyond the general timing/phase model already in place.
examples: "I'm planning on animating this guy landing at least five blows before ending this animation. So, I just keep using those principles to animate, anticipation, action, anticipation, action, and follow-through" - follow-through named only once, after naming two full anticipation-action pairs (video @ 03:45-03:59)

the combo's actual ending is escalated beyond an ordinary follow-through into a full finishing move (a suplex), preceded by its own dedicated anticipation ("before the suplex... I'm going to animate him go lower to get a better grip... this is our anticipation pose") (video @ 04:01-04:26)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/4uvQytZ3DmA @ 03:45-04:26 - Besty Animates states the repeated anticipation-action cadence and the single deferred follow-through directly while narrating a five-hit combo's construction in Clip Studio Paint; the specific combo frames themselves fall in an unsampled stretch of this session's 100-frame sample (dominated by unrelated B-roll and channel bumpers), so this rests on the transcript's explicit description rather than a directly-viewed sequence; experimental until validated
